title: What Brain Freeze Does Inside Your Head
description:
Something ice cold hits the roof of your mouth, a big blood vessel feeding your brain suddenly widens, and the pressure inside your skull rises. The twist: the nerve that reports that pain also covers your forehead, so your brain blames your forehead. Press your tongue to the roof of your mouth or sip something warm and it fades in seconds.

Does it get you too?

Sources: Serrador et al., presentation at Experimental Biology 2012 (reported by ScienceDaily and the American Physiological Society); Cleveland Clinic, "Brain Freeze (Ice Cream Headache)"; NBC News, "Brain freeze: why ice cream makes some scream".
For curiosity only, not medical advice.
